_how_to_add_a_car: Copy one block under 'models', change it, set enabled to true, push. The next run searches for it.
match: every regex must appear in the ad title or address (lower case, hyphens read as spaces).
none: none of these may appear. make: must appear too.
generations: one per chassis/year range. 'name' is what the app shows (E46 M3, AP1 S2000...).
name_by_body: optional, picks the name from the body (E90/E92/E93 M3).
smg_risk: true when an automated gearbox existed, so the ad text must also say manual.
bodies: the bodies this car came in; the first one is used when the ad does not say.
trims: [regex, label] pairs, first match wins.

comps: optional, sold prices from Bring a Trailer. bat = id(s) of the model's results page (open e.g. bringatrailer.com/bmw/e46-m3/ and find keyword_pages in the page source); match = regex the auction title must contain; body = body when the title does not say.
searches: search pages to read every day, per site.
none_body: regexes on the body the listing page states (Coupe, Hatchback...): a match drops the ad.
split: optional, a version priced on its own with its own chip (FA5 Civic Si): match on the title or trim, family, name, color; body forces the body (Brazil's FB Civic Si was only a coupe).
code: optional regex for the chassis code in an ad's title (S13, FD, R34): it picks that generation even a year outside its range.
body: optional on a generation or split, the only body it came in (MR2 Spyder: conv).
brand: the make the app groups the model chips under (Acura NSX in Canada, Honda NSX in Brazil).

bodies on a generation: the only bodies it takes, so one model can split by body (Z3 M Roadster vs Z3 M Coupe) or by year (the 2012-2013 335i sedan is an F30: E9X 335i 2012-2013 lists coupe and conv only).
Bodies: coupe, conv, sedan, wagon, hatch (FK8 Civic Type R, GR STI, 180SX).
recheck: true on the models of a new batch: ads rejected earlier whose address names one get opened once more.
